Quiz1AMSC5710
1. 10 points (Test on XPS: spectra interpretation)
In the XPS measurement of a 200 nm Titanium oxide thin film, we did two XPS survey scans
in order to determine the Ti/O ratio. The first surface scan is performed right after the sample
is loaded in the vacuum, and the second one is performed after the film is sputtered by Ar for
20 seconds. We found that the first survey scan suggests a Ti/O ratio close to 0.5, but also
with a C concentration about 15%. The second survey gives only trace amount of C (<1%),
but with Ti/O ratio significantly differ from 0.5. Can you explain the experimental
observations, and comment on the real composition of the Titanium oxide thin film.

4 points
Show that the Atomic Packing Factor ofa hexagonal close-packed crystal structure is

4 points
Hand sketch a (1ii) plane and a (111) plane within the same cubic unit cell

4 points
Sodium chloride has a rock salt crystal structure. Show that in the unit cell of sodium

General information
Assessment methods
Class works/Quizzes
Taking place in individual seminars (during class). No make up, all counted.
Classroom Presentations
Taking place in the last two weeks of the teaching semester. 2o groups will be formed for Group
presentation (3~4 students per group). Grouping is on random base and carried out by TA.
Each presentation includes 1o min talk +3 min Q&A. This is a very concise presentation with in-
depth analysis of one important problem in a specific field of interest. Presentation topics are
provided (first come first serve).
Essay
Due one week after the last official teaching day of the course (Dec. 3rd). 25 groups will be
formed for Group essay (2~3 students per group, students who were grouped together in the
presentation grouping will be avoided for essay grouping). Essay topics are provided (first come
first serve). Maximum 5 pages text (figure pages not counted), single spacing, 12 font.
Contribution from individual student needs to be elaborated.

COURSEOUTCOMES
Learning Outcomes:
(1) To learn the basic principles of surface science.
(2) To know the technologies that are related to thin films.
(3) To understand the basic principles of vacuum science and technology that are related to surface science and thin-film
deposition techniques.
(4) To understand the thermodynamics of evaporation and learn the basic principles of evaporation.
(5) To acquire the basic knowledge about adsorption, surface diffusion, nucleation, and structure development that are involved
in thin-film deposition.
(6) To acquire the basic knowledge of epitaxial deposition.
(7) To learn the basic knowledge of chemical vapor deposition.
(8) To learn the basic techniques of measuring the physical and chemical properties of thin films.
Course Syllabus:
1: Introduction to Surface Science and Thin Film Technology
2: Vacuum Science and Technology
3: Surface Science
4:Evaporation
5: Deposition
6: Epitaxy
7: Chemical Vapor Deposition
8: Analysis and Properties of Thin Films
